name: Decode-phase GEMM: memory-bandwidth bound at batch size 1
arithmetic_intensity: At batch size 1, the GEMM is memory-bandwidth bound: each weight is loaded from HBM and used for only one multiply-accumulate. The arithmetic intensity is ~1 flop/byte, far below the GPU's ridge point.
workarounds: Weight-only quantization (INT4, FP4) reduces bytes per weight, directly improving memory-bound throughput
Batching increases arithmetic intensity but reduces throughput for interactive workloads
Speculative decoding increases effective batch size for the target model
MoE routing reduces active parameters per token
notes: HARDWARE PARAMETERS, NOT RECORD IDS. 2026-10-04: affected_by_hardware previously held ['memory_bandwidth', 'l2_cache_size', 'tensor_core_count'] - hardware quantities, not products. They could never resolve, so the repo was carrying permanent false debt against a budget that exists to catch NEW bad references. Moved into this note; the field is now EMPTY and that is the correct value, not a gap. Why: These were hardware PARAMETERS (memory_bandwidth, l2_cache_size, tensor_core_count), not products. The record is part-independent too - it is a kernel-level argument citing the Marlin repo, so naming a GPU would invent a dependency it does not claim. The record's own point is that memory bandwidth, L2 size and tensor-core count are the variables that SET the ridge point on any part.
